description: Side-by-side screenshot of two Twitter account-status panels, apparently from an internal moderation tool or account-status checker, with the account names, handles and bio text blacked out. The left account shows follower/count stats, tags reading Perm Suspended, Suspended, Bounced and Protected, and a join date of December 2007. The right account shows a blank avatar and tags reading Bounced, Inactive, Protected, Compromised, Trends Blacklist, Search Blacklist and ReadOnly. description: Official government portrait of Christopher Wray, Director of the FBI (2017-present at the time of the post). He wears a dark pinstripe suit, white shirt, red patterned tie and an American-flag lapel pin, posed before a U.S. flag with gold fringe. Filename on the post: Chris_Wray.jpg.

The official FBI portrait of Director Christopher Wray with a large red X drawn across his face and torso. The underlying image is the same government portrait (dark pinstripe suit, red tie, U.S. flag backdrop); the X overlay signals rejection or removal of Wray, consistent with Q-post usage marking officials as targeted for dismissal.
flags: The red X conveys the poster's editorial claim/judgment about Wray, not a factual event
